name: Bansal and Başar's two-point design, $f(x)=\sigma\sqrt{2/\pi}\,\mathrm{sgn}(x)$
method: Two-point design whose level minimizes the first-stage cost
notes: Bansal and Başar take $f(x)=\varepsilon\,\mathrm{sgn}(x)$ and report a cost of $0.363$ in the limit $k\to 0$ with $k\sigma = 1$, against $0.404$ for Witsenhausen's $\varepsilon=\sigma$. That limit is reached with $\varepsilon=\sigma\sqrt{2/\pi}=\mathbb{E}|x_0|$, the level that minimizes the first-stage cost, $k^2\sigma^2(1-2/\pi)\approx 0.3634$. At the benchmark the second stage adds about $0.0016$, so $0.363$ is not this controller's cost here.
